topics.topic: How agent sessions become known to Registry and visible to the owner
questions: How does Registry come to know a session so the owner can pick it and Registry can refuse an unknown one? No action registers or lists agent sessions.
How does Registry learn of agent sessions, and how does the owner see which sessions exist in order to choose for one? No action registers or lists sessions.
Which action makes an agent session known to Registry, so that the owner can choose a project for it? Who performs that action, Kernel or the owner?

quotes: unknown or archived project refused; unknown session refused
There is no global working project.
names a session, and what ends one, belong to State 2.
judgement.divergence: One implementation has Kernel register each agent session with Registry and lists the sessions to the owner. Another has the owner type a session identifier, and Registry accepts any well-formed one. The owner notices when choosing a working project, and Kernel notices whether it must register first.
judgement.why: The owner must choose a project for a known session and an unknown session is refused, yet no primary action makes a session known or shows the owner which sessions exist; State 2 is given only how Kernel names a session.

topics.topic: How the agent names a target project in a switch request without the catalogue, what refusal reveals, and how archived targets are handled
questions: How does the agent name a target project when it never sees the catalogue, and does 'unknown project refused' disclose to the agent which projects exist? What happens when the target is archived?
How does the agent name a target project without seeing the catalogue, and does answering 'unknown project' reveal to the agent which ids exist?

The agent never sees the catalogue. How does it name the project it asks to switch to? Does the request carry a project_id, or free text the owner resolves? Is a request for an archived project refused?

quotes: a pending request of that session the owner sees in the owner interface, replacing the session's earlier pending one; the working context does not change (R0-42)
creates no project and never sees the catalogue (R0-41)
Through Cabinet Kernel the agent reads and writes only the project the owner
judgement.divergence: One implementation takes a project_id in the switch request, refuses unknown ids and so tells the agent which ids exist, and accepts archived targets as pending. Another takes free text that the owner resolves, never confirms existence to the agent, and refuses archived targets. The agent (through Kernel) and the owner notice.
judgement.why: The switch request names a target project, but the texts never say how an agent without the catalogue names it, whether the refusal may reveal which projects exist, or whether an archived target is refused.

topics.topic: What 'read a project' and 'list projects' return to a service whose token does not allow personal_data
questions: The card includes the object's address, which is personal_data. What does a service whose token does not allow personal_data receive, given that R0-26 forbids mixed answers?
What project card and list items does a service whose token stops below personal_data receive (object, address, customer, name)? R0-26 forbids mixed answers.

What does a service whose token does not allow `personal_data` get from 'read a project' and 'list projects', given that the card holds the object's address and R0-26 forbids mixed answers? Is the request refused, or is the service given a projection without personal values?

quotes: owner; a trusted service, in its disclosure class (R0-26)
the project card (any status, V1-7) with its object and rooms, its revision; the project's id stands at the top of the answer (R0-13)
An answer that contains a `personal_data` value is never `open`
caller needs both, Registry offers separate outputs or a dedicated projection
judgement.divergence: One implementation refuses 'read a project' and 'list projects' to a service whose token stops below personal_data. Another returns that service a card or list without the object's address and other personal values. Consumer services such as Cabinet notice.
judgement.why: The card holds personal_data and mixed answers are forbidden, but the texts leave open whether a lower-class service is refused or served a projection.

topics.topic: Where Cabinet Kernel, PresuPro, Cabinet and the owner interface run, and over which channel each reaches the production service API
questions: Where do Cabinet Kernel, PresuPro and Cabinet run, and over which channel does each reach the production service API? Only Client Portal's WireGuard path is named, and no agent may run on the production host.
Where do PresuPro, Cabinet and Cabinet Kernel run, and how do they reach the production Registry? The WireGuard tunnel is described only for Portal, and no agent runs on the home server.

Where do Cabinet Kernel, Cabinet and PresuPro run, and how do they reach the service API? The only named channel carries Portal's traffic from the VPS. And how does the owner interface reach the internet over HTTPS from the home server, which publishes no port?

From where is the owner interface reachable remotely: the home LAN, a VPN, or the public internet through a port the home server publishes? R0-39 says the home server publishes no listening port to the internet.

quotes: reachable only on the production host and over that channel.
The tunnel carries the service API only
tunnel that the home server initiates; the home server publishes no listening
the interface is reachable only through HTTPS
judgement.divergence: One implementation runs Kernel, PresuPro and Cabinet on the VPS through the WireGuard tunnel and reaches the owner interface only via the tunnel or the home LAN. Another runs those services on the home server and publishes an HTTPS port to the internet. Kernel, PresuPro, Cabinet and the owner, who reaches the interface remotely, notice.
judgement.why: Only Portal's channel is named; the location and channel of the other services, and the owner interface's remote path given that no port is published, are unnamed trust boundaries.

topics.topic: Whether Kernel's publish, withdraw and read-latest for the agent are confined to the session's project, and what failure applies otherwise
questions: Can Kernel acting for the agent read the latest artifact of any project, or only on its session's project, as R0-41 requires?
The table does not confine Kernel's publish and withdraw to the session's project, but R0-41 does. Which text governs, and what failure does a publish on another project produce?
Are publish and withdraw by Kernel confined to the session's project (R0-41), with a failure for another project? The table states no such confinement or failure for either action.
Can Kernel for the agent read the latest pointer of any project, or only of its session's project as R0-41 and R0-32 require?
Are publish, withdraw and read-latest by Cabinet Kernel for the agent confined to the session's project, as R0-41 requires? These rows say 'a service' or 'producer service' without that limit.

quotes: agent authority on a project are confined to the project of the current context;
Through Cabinet Kernel the agent reads and writes only the project the owner
project, lists and adds its rooms, publishes and withdraws Kernel's pointers on
judgement.why: R0-32 and R0-41 confine every operation Kernel performs with agent authority, publish, withdraw and read-latest included, to the session's project; the less specific table rows do not widen that.

topics.topic: Whether R0-45, proposed with no objection, has the standing of an owner decision
questions: R0-45 is 'proposed to the owner ... no objection', not an owner answer. Does silence count as an owner decision under R0-15, or is R0-45 pending until the owner accepts it?
Is a proposal met with no objection an owner decision of the same standing as the other R0 entries?
R0-45 was 'proposed to the owner ... no objection', not answered by the owner. Is it an owner decision under R0-15, or still open until the owner confirms it?

quotes: State 0 closes again when its question rounds are clear; the owner
The whole of this document, not only the numbered owner decisions, is the
judgement.why: Whatever standing R0-45 has now, the owner accepts the whole document, R0-45 included, when State 0 closes.

topics.topic: Whether the `customer` field of `context` carries only the customer_ref or also contact data
questions: Does the `customer` field of `context`, sent to PresuPro and Client Portal, carry only the `customer_ref`, or contact data such as the name? If it carries contact data, this sentence contradicts R0-43.
Does the `customer` field of `context`, served to PresuPro and Client Portal, carry only the customer_ref or any contact data (for example the name)?

Does `context` (and the project card) give a trusted service with `personal_data` allowed the customer's contact data? R0-26 lets `personal_data` reach such a service, R0-43 hands it `context` with 'customer', and this line says contact data reaches the owner alone.

quotes: The customer's contact data reaches the owner alone.
the snapshot a consumer keeps: id, display name, status, address, customer, created and updated times (R0-04)
`context` keeps its fields (R0-04) and answers only a trusted service whose
owner and to a service whose token allows that class (R0-27) — never to an agent
judgement.divergence: One implementation's `context` carries only the customer_ref. Another's carries the customer's name or other contact data to PresuPro and Client Portal. Those services and the owner notice.
judgement.why: The texts let personal_data reach services that are allowed it, yet say contact data reaches the owner alone, so what `context`'s customer field discloses is left open.

topics.topic: Which action records the end of a customer relationship, and who erases or anonymises data when retention expires
questions: Which action records that a relationship has ended, and who performs it? Which actor and action erase or anonymise data when a period ends, with what observable output and audit entry? The table has no row for either.
Which action records that a relationship ended, starting the retention clock? Its representation is carried to State 1, but no primary action carries it.
Which action records that a customer relationship ended, and who performs it? Is the end derived instead, for example from all of the customer's projects being archived?

quotes: A customer's contact data: until the relationship with the customer ends,
end of a customer relationship is recorded, and what an anonymised project,
When a period ends the data is erased or anonymised, respecting the mandatory
judgement.divergence: One implementation has the owner record the end of a relationship through an explicit action. Another derives the end, for example from all of the customer's projects being archived. The owner notices when contact data disappears and whether there is an action to perform.
judgement.why: The retention clock depends on the end of a relationship, but no primary action or actor records that end; State 1 is given only its representation.

topics.topic: Which operations count as significant for R0-37 audit
questions: Which operations are significant? Are reads of personal data and refused requests included? This is not carried to a later state.
Which operations are significant: all writes, reads of personal data, refusals, context reads? This is not carried to a later state.
Which operations are significant? Are services' reads of personal data, agent projection reads and failed or refused requests included?

judgement.why: Which operations count as significant for the audit log is a rule with its required tests, and rules belong to State 2.

topics.topic: What observable behaviour restricting processing of a customer changes
questions: Contact data already reaches the owner alone. What observable behaviour does restriction change: list visibility, use in new or existing projects, appearance in context, or the retention clock?

What does a restriction change in observable behaviour, given that contact data already reaches the owner alone? Does it block naming the customer in projects, the customer_ref in `context`, or something else?

quotes: the Customer marked restricted: its contact data stays stored but leaves Registry to no one but the owner (R0-37)
The customer's contact data reaches the owner alone.
project? Recommended: the owner lifts it; correction and erasure stay
judgement.divergence: One implementation makes restriction only a marker, because contact data already reaches the owner alone. Another blocks naming the customer in new projects, or drops the customer from `context`. The owner and PresuPro or Client Portal notice.
judgement.why: The promise of restriction has no observable output distinct from the unrestricted state, and OQ-14 covers only part of what it changes.

topics.topic: Whether import keeps source customer_ref, room and pointer identities or remaps them, and how collisions are handled
questions: Does an import keep the source's customer_ref, room ids and pointer ids and versions? R0-16 says a caller never supplies a customer_ref, and Registry mints room and pointer identities. What happens when an imported customer_ref collides with one production holds?
Does import keep the source's customer_ref and pointer and room ids, contrary to R0-16 (Registry mints customer_ref, never caller-supplied), or are new ones minted and remapped?

quotes: the project under the identity it carries in its source, with its customer, object, rooms and pointers (R0-34, R0-44)
by the running instances included (migration) — and it keeps its links:
a caller never supplies one, and recording the same person twice makes two
the export carries (customers and pointers included or not).
judgement.divergence: One implementation keeps the source's customer_ref, room ids and pointer ids and versions on import. Another mints new ones and remaps them. Consumers that hold room ids taken from the project card, and the owner after a customer_ref collision, notice.
judgement.why: Import keeps the project's identity and links, but the texts never say whether the linked customer, room and pointer identities are kept or reminted, or what happens on a customer_ref collision.

topics.topic: Whether onboard_object is retired or gets a service token, and which of its role Kernel flows take
questions: With every request authenticated (R0-27) and the owner credential held by no tool (R0-30), does onboard_object get a service token, or is it retired?
onboard_object created projects and customers, but R0-41 says Kernel no longer creates projects. Which part of that role, if any, do Kernel flows take?

quotes: The operator script `onboard_object`: a client of the API like any consumer,
designed elsewhere; its staff-credential use ends with R0-30, and its role is
taken by the owner interface and Kernel flows.
judgement.why: onboard_object is excluded and designed elsewhere, its credential use ends, and its role passes to the owner interface and Kernel flows within their own limits.
